So let's review. Last class we discussed the mission of Jesus. Who is Jesus? Jesus was a messenger from the monad who reminded us that there's a divine spark in us, and how you activate the divine spark is by focusing on Jesus and repeating his words. Jesus was like Zoroaster, like Plato, like Homer, like Yahweh—a poor prophet. And so if you just repeated his sayings or poetry, then you could activate that spark within you and you could glow. This explains why it became popular. It also explains why the Romans had to kill him because at this time in history, the Roman Empire's main currency and economy were based on slavery.

Most people were slaves; if they weren't, they were poor. And here is Jesus who came to remind you that you don't have to be a slave—you are free to do whatever you want. There's a higher power than the Roman Empire: it is the divine or the universe. This is why people started to defy their masters and no longer feared death. The Romans had to kill Jesus because he was "stealing" slaves, making them free.

Now the question is, how did we get from Jesus to the Catholic Church? Jesus taught us that we are free to believe whatever we want; just listen to our hearts as we would be in touch with the monad again and have nothing to fear. The Catholic Church teaches us that you must believe in Jesus to achieve redemption and salvation because he came to die for our sins, making us slaves to him. These are two opposite ideas: the divine spark is the greatest threat to the Roman Empire, so they imprisoned it by creating the Catholic Church as a means to control it and hide it from you. The main architect of this church was Paul, who most people believe founded Christianity.

Paul had an interesting background—he was a Jew raised in Greek culture, very well educated, and wealthy. He's called a hellenized Jew and might have worked for the Roman Empire as a spy or agent. Education back then mainly focused on rhetoric—sophistry. Sophists believed that words are reality, while philosophers believed they were illusions. Paul's trick was to change focus from listening to Jesus's words to believing in him, thereby constructing Christianity by synthesizing Roman, Greek, and Jewish cultures.

Remember the Bible is heavily influenced by Persian culture at this time, and Paul tells us Jesus is the promised Messiah.
